1.explanation: Both of the React files that render tabs need to participate in the truncation behavior. Tabs.js is where we add the “container” modifier class to the outer wrapper, but it never tells the individual tab links to clip their text for that variant. Tab.js is where each <a> element is rendered with the standard nav-link class and tooltip title, but it doesn’t detect the container type and apply any CSS class or inline style that would trigger text-overflow: ellipsis at 16px. To fix it, you’d augment Tabs.js to pass a prop or additional class down when type === 'container', and update Tab.js to apply the clipping style (or hook into the existing CSS) for that class on the <a> so long labels get truncated the way default tabs do.
1.bug_scenario: When you use the React “container” variant of Tabs, long tab labels are allowed to overflow the container rather than being truncated and showing an ellipsis 16px from the edge, as they do in the default (non-container) tabs. In the screenshot you can see “Tab label 1 long name” running right up against the edge instead of being clipped with “…” like the default tabs do.
